about: Doom Scroll clip cards (Phase 3, Nov 6 2026): short segments of real AWS videos, each followed by one question about what the segment showed. Only official AWS YouTube channels (Amazon Web Services, AWS Events). Every youtubeId was verified on the date given: oEmbed returned 200, the watch page reported status OK and playableInEmbed true, and start/end were chosen from the video's own captions. Times are seconds; segments run 45 to 150 seconds. module = exact module title in courses/aws-saa-c03.js; topic = exact topic title in that module (optional).

clips.topic: The Financial Shift: CapEx vs OpEx
clips.title: Trading CapEx for OpEx
clips.why: Listen for the exact phrase AWS uses for the money shift, capital expense traded for variable expense, and what deploying globally in minutes buys you.

q.q: According to the narrator, what does cloud computing let you trade?
opts: Variable expense for fixed monthly fees
Regional capacity for a single data center
q.exp: You stop making large upfront investments in hardware and pay for IT as you consume it; the clip also notes you can grow or shrink capacity instantly and deploy to new Regions in minutes.

clips.source: What is Cloud Computing? | Amazon Web Services

clips.title: Inside an AWS Region (re:Invent 2024)
clips.why: Watch for how far apart Availability Zones sit, what they do not share, and why AWS deploys changes one AZ at a time.

q.q: How far apart does the speaker say Availability Zones are kept within a Region?
opts: In the same building, on separate racks
About 60 miles (100 km) apart, on separate flood plains and power grids
At least 1,000 km apart, in different countries
Exactly 10 km apart, sharing one electrical grid
q.exp: AZs are meaningfully distant (about 60 miles) with separate flood plains, electrical grids, power and cooling so one disaster cannot take out two of them, yet close enough to keep latency inside the Region low. Service changes roll out one AZ at a time for the same reason.

clips.source: AWS re:Invent 2024 - Anatomy of an AWS Region (ARC204)

clips.title: Sticky sessions on the load balancer
clips.why: Watch why one instance is a bad idea, why adding instances needs a load balancer, and what the ELB trick for keeping a user's session is called.

q.q: What does the clip call the load balancer setting that keeps sending one user to the same EC2 instance?
q.exp: Sticky sessions pin a session to one instance with a single checkbox. Simple, but if that server dies its sessions are lost, which is why the episode later moves session data into ElastiCache.

clips.source: Back to Basics: Managing Your Web Application's Session

clips.title: Auto Scaling that follows the demand curve
clips.why: Catch which scaling policy the speaker recommends, which metrics it tracks, and the two other policy types he names.

q.q: Which scaling policy does the speaker strongly recommend for following demand?
opts: Target tracking on a metric like average CPU or request count per target
Scaling only on EC2 status checks
q.exp: Target tracking keeps a metric at the value you choose (around 70% CPU for availability, 40% for cost, or a mix); step scaling uses CloudWatch alarm bounds and predictive scaling forecasts the next 48 hours from history.

clips.source: Back to Basics: Designing for Failure with EC2

clips.title: Whiteboarding your first VPC
clips.why: Watch what gives a public subnet its internet path, what controls traffic between subnets, and which gateway reaches your data center.

q.q: On the whiteboard, what gives the public subnet access to and from the internet?
opts: A NAT gateway in the private subnet
The internet gateway on the VPC
q.exp: Public subnets route through the internet gateway; the private subnet talks to the public one through VPC routing, policed by network ACLs and security groups; the virtual private gateway is for VPN tunnels or Direct Connect back to your data center.

clips.source: AWS SA Whiteboarding | Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)

clips.title: PrivateLink: services that appear inside your VPC
clips.why: Listen for where the traffic travels and which three things you no longer need once it stays on the AWS network.

q.q: With AWS PrivateLink, which of these does the clip say your VPC no longer needs to reach a service?
opts: An internet gateway, NAT device or public IP address
q.exp: PrivateLink routes traffic between VPCs and services over the AWS network, so no internet gateway, NAT device or public IP is required; it also works over Direct Connect for on-premises access.

clips.source: AWS PrivateLink

clips.title: A resilient VPC baseline
clips.why: Count the minimum Availability Zones, notice the warning about IP ranges, and spot the shared-exit pattern for internet traffic.

q.q: What pattern does the clip suggest for outbound internet traffic from many VPCs?
opts: A NAT gateway in every subnet of every VPC
VPC peering to a single bastion host
A Transit Gateway with a shared egress VPC holding the NAT and internet gateways
q.exp: Transit Gateway handles inter-VPC traffic and one egress VPC centralizes the NAT and internet gateways instead of duplicating them per VPC; the VPC itself should span at least two AZs with an IP range that will not overlap partners.

clips.source: Back to Basics: Start Your AWS Journey with a Resilient Infrastructure Baseline Architecture

clips.title: EC2 and the Nitro hypervisor
clips.why: Notice what the Nitro System is described as: a lightweight hypervisor that offloads virtualization work to dedicated hardware.

q.q: What does the clip say the AWS Nitro System does?
opts: Offloads virtualization functions to dedicated hardware so instances get nearly all of the server's resources
Stores instance data on S3 for durability
Caches web content at edge locations
q.exp: Nitro is the lightweight hypervisor under modern EC2; it hands practically all the server's resources to your instances, which also run on AWS Graviton and other specialized chips.

clips.source: What is Amazon EC2? | Amazon Web Services

clips.title: Lambda in 90 seconds
clips.why: Notice what Lambda scales on and what you pay for.

q.q: According to the clip, how does Lambda scale?
opts: You add instances to an Auto Scaling group
It scales once a day on a schedule
Automatically, up and down with incoming requests
You choose a fixed number of servers per Region
q.exp: Lambda runs code without provisioning servers, scales automatically with incoming requests and bills only for the resources you use.

clips.source: AWS Lambda explained in 90 seconds | Amazon Web Services

clips.topic: EC2 Cost Optimization: Reserved, Spot & Savings Plans
clips.title: Two rules of Spot Instances
clips.why: Catch what defines a Spot pool and how much warning you get before an interruption.

q.q: How much warning does EC2 give before reclaiming a Spot Instance?
q.exp: Each instance type, size and Availability Zone is its own Spot pool with its own price; when AWS needs the capacity back you get a two-minute warning in the instance status and metadata.

clips.source: Amazon EC2 Spot Instances: Spot Rules

clips.title: EBS volume types and snapshots
clips.why: Note which volume type is the balanced default and which one is named for latency-sensitive databases.

q.q: Which EBS volume does the clip pair with SAP HANA, Oracle and SQL Server?
q.exp: gp3 balances price and performance for everyday transactional workloads; io2 Block Express delivers consistent sub-millisecond latency for the demanding databases. Snapshots give point-in-time copies for DR and cross-Region migration.

clips.source: Introduction to Amazon EBS | Amazon Web Services

clips.title: The three Glacier classes
clips.why: Match each Glacier class to its retrieval time as the narrator walks down the price ladder.

q.q: Which Glacier class returns data in milliseconds?
q.exp: Instant Retrieval is milliseconds, Flexible Retrieval is minutes to hours (backups, DR), Deep Archive is hours at the lowest cost in the cloud (compliance archives); all three offer 11 nines of durability.

clips.source: Introduction to the Amazon S3 Glacier Storage Classes | Amazon Web Services

clips.title: EFS: one file system, many instances
clips.why: Catch the protocol EFS speaks, how it is billed, and where it keeps copies of your data.

q.q: What protocol does the clip say Amazon EFS uses?
q.exp: EFS is a shared NFSv4 file system for EC2: many instances mount it at once, it grows and shrinks automatically, you pay only for space used, and data is replicated across multiple AZs in the Region.

clips.source: Introduction to Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) - Cloud File Storage on AWS

clips.title: RDS Multi-AZ: one standby or two
clips.why: Count the Availability Zones each option spans and compare the two failover times.

q.q: What does the two-readable-standby option add over one standby?
opts: Three AZs, read endpoints and failover typically under 35 seconds
A single AZ with faster disks
q.exp: One standby replicates synchronously to a second AZ with failover as quick as 60 seconds; two readable standbys span three AZs, add read capacity and lower write latency, and fail over in under 35 seconds. Both give zero data loss.

clips.source: Introduction to Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployments | Amazon Web Services

clips.title: DynamoDB at any scale
clips.why: Catch the latency promise, the pricing model and the multi-Region feature.

q.q: What does the clip say about DynamoDB performance as the workload grows?
opts: Latency doubles with each table partition
It needs a read replica per Region
Performance depends on the instance size you pick
Consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale
q.exp: DynamoDB is serverless NoSQL with single-digit millisecond latency at any scale, on-demand pay-per-request pricing, built-in multi-AZ replication and global tables for multi-Region, multi-active deployments.

clips.source: What is Amazon DynamoDB? | Amazon Web Services

clips.topic: ElastiCache: The Caching Layer (Redis vs Memcached)
clips.title: ElastiCache for Redis
clips.why: Note why in-memory beats disk and how Redis scales reads versus writes.

q.q: How does the clip say ElastiCache for Redis scales writes?
q.exp: In-memory data is orders of magnitude faster than disk; replicas scale reads across AZs, partitioning (cluster mode) scales writes, and Multi-AZ auto failover promotes a replica when a node dies.

clips.source: Introduction to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis

clips.title: Fan-out with SNS
clips.why: Watch why point-to-point connections fall apart at scale and which service AWS names for pub/sub fan-out.

q.q: In the pub/sub model shown, what happens when a publisher sends a message to a topic?
opts: It waits in a queue until one consumer polls it
It is written to DynamoDB first
It is immediately pushed to every subscriber of the topic
The publisher must call each subscriber's API
q.exp: A topic is the logical access point; SNS fans each message out to every subscriber, with retries and failure handling built in, so publishers and subscribers never need to know about each other.

clips.source: Back to Basics: Building Fan-Out Serverless Architectures Using SNS, SQS and Lambda

clips.title: Step Functions in 90 seconds
clips.why: Note what Step Functions tracks between steps and what it removes from your functions.

q.q: What does the clip say Step Functions takes care of so your code does not have to?
opts: State checkpoints, error handling and restarts between workflow steps
q.exp: Step Functions is serverless orchestration: it breaks a workflow into steps, adds flow logic, tracks inputs and outputs, and handles checkpoints, errors and restarts in a visual workflow.

clips.source: AWS Step Functions explained in 90 seconds | Amazon Web Services

clips.title: Commands vs events, and the event bus
clips.why: Catch the difference between a directed command and an observable event, and what the bus rules do for a newly added service.

q.q: In the clip, what is the key difference between a command and an event?
opts: A command is asynchronous; an event is synchronous
Events must be acknowledged with a 201; commands are fire-and-forget
Commands use SQS; events use SNS
A command targets a specific recipient; an event is simply observable by anyone listening
q.exp: Producers emit events without knowing the consumers; the EventBridge bus applies rules to route and filter events to targets, so a new service adds a rule instead of asking the producer team for changes.

clips.source: Intro to Amazon EventBridge

clips.title: Route 53 and Traffic Flow
clips.why: Catch the availability figure and what Traffic Flow does for an application running in several Regions.

q.q: What does Route 53 Traffic Flow do, according to the clip?
opts: Sends each user to the best location and fails over to an alternate endpoint
Caches web pages at edge locations
Load-balances TCP traffic inside a VPC
q.exp: Route 53 is DNS with 100% availability; Traffic Flow routes users to the best location for them and re-routes to an alternate location when the primary endpoint becomes unavailable.

clips.source: Amazon Route 53

clips.title: CloudFront in 100 seconds
clips.why: Note what comes with CloudFront at no charge: Shield Standard, ACM certificates and data transfer from AWS origins.

q.q: What does the clip say about data transfer from other AWS origins to CloudFront?
opts: It costs the same as internet egress
It is billed per edge location
It requires a Direct Connect link
q.exp: CloudFront delivers static and dynamic content from edge locations; you get Shield Standard DDoS protection, free ACM TLS certificates, WAF integration and Lambda@Edge, and no charge for data transfer out from other AWS origins to CloudFront.

clips.source: Introduction to Amazon CloudFront

clips.title: Transit Gateway: one big cloud router
clips.why: Listen for what Transit Gateway connects and the analogy AWS uses for it.

q.q: How does the clip describe AWS Transit Gateway?
opts: One big cloud router connecting VPCs, VPNs and Direct Connect to a single gateway
A DNS resolver for hybrid networks
q.exp: Transit Gateway centralizes connectivity for hundreds of VPCs, VPNs, accounts and Direct Connect, even across Regions over the AWS global network, with Network Manager for a single view of it all.

clips.source: What is AWS Transit Gateway - Design and Build Your Network Around a Central Hub

clips.topic: Hybrid Connectivity: Site-to-Site VPN vs Direct Connect
clips.title: Direct Connect vs VPN, on the whiteboard
clips.why: Catch the bandwidth increments and where the physical cross-connect into AWS happens.

q.q: Where is the physical cross-connect into AWS made for Direct Connect?
opts: At a Direct Connect partner facility colocated near AWS
q.exp: VPN is quick and runs over the internet; Direct Connect is a dedicated line (1 or 10 Gbps increments) into a partner facility that cross-connects into AWS, terminating in one or more VPCs over 802.1Q VLANs.

clips.source: AWS SA Whiteboarding | AWS Direct Connect

clips.title: IAM in two minutes
clips.why: Catch what permissions apply to, how an existing directory plugs in, and what IAM costs.

q.q: How does the clip say you can reuse an existing identity system like Active Directory with AWS?
opts: Copying users into IAM by hand
q.exp: IAM permissions apply to individual API calls (who, which action, which resource); federation lets admins and developers administer AWS with existing identities, CloudTrail logs the activity, and IAM has no additional charge.

clips.source: Introduction to AWS IAM - Identity and Access Management on AWS

clips.title: KMS in 90 seconds
clips.why: Catch what governs access to a key, where keys are protected, and which service records every key use.

q.q: According to the clip, what controls when, how and who can use a KMS key?
q.exp: KMS keys are generated and protected in FIPS 140 validated hardware security modules; the key policy governs access, asymmetric key pairs sign and verify data, and CloudTrail records every key management action and use.

clips.source: What is AWS Key Management Service? | Amazon Web Services

clips.title: Shield Standard vs Shield Advanced
clips.why: Catch what every AWS customer gets automatically and what the paid tier adds on top.

q.q: Which of these does the clip list as a Shield Advanced benefit?
opts: Cost protection against charges from DDoS-related usage spikes
q.exp: Everyone gets automatic protection against common network and transport layer floods; Shield Advanced adds tailored detection, automatic mitigations, the Shield Response Team, WAF and Firewall Manager at no extra cost, and DDoS cost protection.

clips.source: AWS Shield Animated Explainer Video | Amazon Web Services

clips.topic: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store & AWS STS
clips.title: Secrets Manager: retrieve and rotate
clips.why: Catch the anti-pattern the speaker calls out, how the app gets the secret at runtime, and what performs the automatic rotation.

q.q: What does Secrets Manager use to rotate credentials automatically?
opts: A cron job on your EC2 instance
AWS Lambda functions on a schedule
q.exp: Never hardcode credentials; pull them at runtime through the API with an IAM policy on the application role. Rotation runs through Lambda, ready-made for RDS, Aurora, DocumentDB and Redshift and custom for anything else.

clips.source: Back to Basics: Secrets Management

clips.title: Why one AWS account stops working
clips.why: Catch the problems of prod and non-prod sharing an account, then the two foundation OUs and what each holds.

q.q: Which organizational unit does the clip say holds the log-aggregation and security read-only accounts?
q.exp: A single account mixes prod and non-prod, needs complex condition and tag policies and complicates chargeback; AWS Organizations starts with a Security OU (log archive, security read) and an Infrastructure OU (networking, shared services).

clips.source: Back to Basics: Design Patterns for Building AWS Multi-Account Organization

clips.title: X-Ray announced: tracing microservices
clips.why: Catch why traditional debugging fails for microservices and what X-Ray's visual map shows per request.

q.q: What does the clip say X-Ray provides to spot where errors occur?
opts: A list of CloudTrail API events
A visual map of the application with per-request latency, status and downstream calls
q.exp: X-Ray traces requests across EC2, ECS, DynamoDB, Elastic Beanstalk and Lambda, showing latency, HTTP status, error counts and downstream calls on a service map.

clips.source: Announcing AWS X-Ray

clips.title: What ECS takes off your plate
clips.why: Catch what ECS itself costs and what Fargate removes.

q.q: What does the clip say you pay for Amazon ECS itself?
opts: Nothing extra; you pay only for the AWS resources that run your application
q.exp: ECS has no control plane to manage and no additional charge; with Fargate there are no hosts to patch or upgrade, and ECS Anywhere extends it to on-premises.

clips.source: Introduction to Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) | Amazon Web Services

clips.title: Fargate in 45 seconds
clips.why: Note what you stop managing when containers go serverless.

q.q: What does Fargate remove the need for, according to the clip?
opts: Provisioning and managing servers for your containers
q.exp: Fargate runs serverless containers: no servers to manage, it launches tens of thousands of containers quickly and scales to the application's compute requirements.

clips.source: Introduction to AWS Fargate

clips.title: Four DR options and where DRS fits
clips.why: Count the four DR strategies and note which one a storage-replication solution maps to.

q.q: Which DR strategy does the speaker say a storage-replication solution like AWS DRS typically maps to?
q.exp: The four options are backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby and multi-site active-active; DRS replicates at block level into a replication subnet and launches recovery instances only when needed, which is pilot light.

clips.source: Back to Basics: How to Implement a Multi-Region Disaster Recovery Strategy Using AWS DRS

clips.title: Storage Gateway: file, tape, volume
clips.why: Match the three gateway types to the protocol each one presents and where the data lands.

q.q: Which Storage Gateway type presents iSCSI block storage to your application servers?
q.exp: File Gateway offers SMB/NFS shares stored as S3 objects or FSx files, Tape Gateway is a virtual tape library for backup software archiving to Glacier, and Volume Gateway presents iSCSI volumes with EBS snapshots for recovery.

clips.source: AWS Storage Gateway

clips.title: Savings Plans walkthrough
clips.why: Catch the maximum discount, what the recommendations are based on, and the three plan types in the console.

q.q: Which Savings Plan type covers EC2, Fargate and Lambda together?
q.exp: Savings Plans discount on-demand prices by up to 72% for an hourly commitment; Compute plans span EC2, Fargate and Lambda, EC2 Instance plans lock to a family and Region, and the recommendations in Cost Explorer come from your past usage.

clips.source: AWS Cost Optimisation Series: Saving Plans | Amazon Web Services

clips.topic: The Hidden Bill: Data Transfer & NAT Costs
clips.title: Cutting NAT gateway charges
clips.why: Catch the two cheapest fixes: a NAT gateway in the same AZ as the talkers, and gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB.

q.q: If most NAT gateway traffic goes to S3 or DynamoDB in the same Region, what does the clip recommend?
opts: CloudFront in front of the bucket
A gateway VPC endpoint, which has no data processing or hourly charge
q.exp: Put the NAT gateway in the same AZ as the busiest instances to avoid cross-AZ charges, use gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB (free), interface endpoints for other AWS services, and an internet gateway for instances that may sit in a public subnet.

clips.source: How can I reduce data transfer charges for my NAT gateway?

clips.topic: AWS Cost Tools: Explorer, Budgets & Trusted Advisor
clips.title: Trusted Advisor in a minute
clips.why: Catch what Trusted Advisor compares your environment against and the three pillars it names.

q.q: What does the clip say Trusted Advisor compares your environment to?
opts: AWS best practices, producing prioritized recommendations
q.exp: Trusted Advisor checks cost optimization, security and resilience against AWS best practices and benchmarks, with context-driven, prioritized recommendations and guided next steps.

clips.source: AWS Trusted Advisor | Amazon Web Services
